correctness.rationale: Conditioning one excursion on success gives the terminal marks, since the trials are iid and geometrically repeated. The absorbing-interval transform has a near-endpoint term exp(-qd sqrt(1+s)) and an opposite-endpoint term bounded exponentially in q. After z=qd, the local densities are dominated by a constant times z^(beta-1), and the part outside any fixed target neighborhood is exponentially small. This proves the rescaled transform on each side, with a leading coefficient of zero allowed, and p_r ~ (c_+ + c_-) Gamma(beta) q^(-beta). The conditional time transform gives E[U|Z]=Z/2 and Var(U|Z)=Z/4, so Cov(Z,U)=beta/2 and the claimed correlation is 1/sqrt(2) for the limit law. The failed-duration sum is independent of the terminal marks at finite rate; its Laplace transform on the rp_r scale tends to (1+theta)^(-1), while the terminal duration on that scale vanishes. The mean threshold follows from the single-trial elapsed mean (1-p_r)/r. For total variation the coupling can disagree only if the far endpoint is hit first and before reset, with probability sinh(qd)/sinh(2aq). Add the omitted half-line Gamma tail, use ring success mass at least half the untruncated half-line mass for x>=2beta+2, and bound the cost of normalization by twice the unnormalized discrepancy divided by ring success mass. This gives the claimed factor-four bound for the symmetric pure power family, not an exact TV asymptotic.
